model.title: Single-cylinder four-stroke teaching engine
model.description: Unqualified proposal for human review: prescribed slider-crank motion and illustrative timing, not combustion or engine dynamics.
assumptions: Exactly one cylinder; representative four-stroke spark-ignition engine. Dimensions, timing and playback speed are teaching assumptions, not product specifications.
elapsed_time default 0 s, minimum 0 s, maximum 20 s. Scrubbing this clock covers two crankshaft revolutions and one complete cycle.
time_experiment: time_input=elapsed_time; step_seconds=0.02; playback_speed=1; reset_on_change=[]; end_time_id=cycle_duration. Stop at 20 s; parameter changes restart atomically.
Preserve mobile, keyboard, reduced-motion, pause and inspection controls. Never resume a paused experiment automatically.
Coordinates: x lateral, y downward, z along crankshaft; metres. Crank centre is the origin. Piston pin is (0,piston_y); crank pin is (crank_x,crank_y).
Fixed crank radius 0.03 m and connecting-rod pin spacing 0.10 m are illustrative. The rigid rod connects the calculated pin centres.
Initial piston position is top dead centre. Crank angle runs from -pi to pi and wraps between revolutions; wrapping must not produce reverse rotation.
Rod angle is measured from +x toward +y along the piston-pin-to-crank-pin vector. Angle display_scale=57.29577951308232; display_unit=degrees.
Prescribed crankshaft/flywheel frequency is 0.1 Hz; camshaft frequency is 0.05 Hz. These are slow teaching playback rates, not calculated operating speeds.
Stroke intervals in cycle fraction: intake [0,0.25), compression [0.25,0.5), power [0.5,0.75), exhaust [0.75,1]. Final endpoint retains exhaust before stopping.
Ideal intake and exhaust valves open only in their named strokes. Fixed open lift is 0.004 m; switching is instantaneous, with no overlap.

Ignition occurs illustratively at cycle fraction 0.5. ignition_indication marks the power-stroke teaching panel and spark location, not sustained sparking or combustion duration. Annotate the exact ignition boundary explicitly using cycle_fraction and stroke_code; do not depict continuous sparks throughout power stroke playback simply because that panel is active digitized as ignition_indication=1
limitations: Kinematics only: pressure rise, force transmission and rotational inertia are qualitative explanations. Prescribed rotation does not calculate self-sustaining operation.
Exclude two-stroke gas exchange; quantitative torque, power, efficiency, pressure, emissions and thermal predictions; detailed fuel delivery, lubrication and cooling.
No combustion chemistry, compressible gas-flow calculation, engineering cam profile, valve acceleration or validated motorcycle specifications.
Flow cues travel at an arbitrary 0.5 m/s while the corresponding valve is open. They show route and direction, not predicted gas velocity or mass flow.

A simplified timing connection shows camshaft speed at half crankshaft speed. Detailed chain dynamics are excluded; use a stationary connection schematic rather than uncalculated traveling chain motion.
Bounds: fraction 0–1; crank turns 0–2; crank angle -pi–pi; cam angle 0–2pi; crank coordinates ±0.03 m; piston y -0.13 to -0.07 m.
Rod squared vertical span is 0.0091–0.01 m2; direction cosine is -0.3–0.3; rod angle is 1.266–1.876 radians. Denominators are fixed positive.
Flags are 0 or 1; stroke code 0–3; lifts 0–0.004 m; cue speeds 0–0.5 m/s. All calculated magnitudes are below 21; no negative square roots occur.
Trigonometric operands are within ±pi. Cam angle is a rotation binding, not a sin/cos operand.
Downstream cutaway, selectable parts and guided comparisons explain the same state. They add no force, energy or gas-flow predictions.

definition.title: Inside a single-cylinder four-stroke engine
definition.description: A simplified, inspectable motorcycle engine with one cylinder, two valves and a two-revolution teaching cycle.

parts.label: Cycle time
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Default 0 s; range 0–20 s. Playback clock and scrub control for one complete two-revolution cycle.

parts.label: Cycle fraction
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Progress through the complete four-stroke cycle.

parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Cumulative crankshaft revolutions.

parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Piston position above crank centre on x=0.

parts.label: Intake valve open
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Common intake-valve and intake-flow engagement flag.

limits: Teaching geometry, not motorcycle specifications. Exactly one four-stroke, spark-ignition cylinder.
Visual mapping: 100 scene units per metre on every axis; world X=model x, world Y=-model y, world Z=-model z. Equations retain SI units.
Preserve mobile, keyboard, reduced-motion, pause and inspection controls. Never resume playback because the learner is idle.
The 0–20 s illustrative playback stops at cycle_duration and covers two crankshaft turns and one camshaft turn; it is not calculated operating speed.
Intake, compression, power and exhaust follow the accepted stroke_code intervals. Valve lifts switch instantaneously between 0 and 0.004 m, without overlap.
Ignition is annotated only at cycle_fraction=0.5, the start of stroke_code=2. The power-panel flag must not create continuous sparks.
Kinematics only. Combustion pressure, force transmission and rotational inertia are explained qualitatively; self-sustaining operation is not calculated.

Exclude two-stroke gas exchange; quantitative torque, power, efficiency, pressure, emissions and thermal predictions; detailed fuel delivery, lubrication and cooling; combustion chemistry and compressible flow calculations. No validated engineering cam profile or valve acceleration is modeled, and no motorcycle specifications are verified here. Teaching playback is prescribed, not calculated from,

parts.label: Engine stand
parts.explanation: The stand holds the engine upright so we can look inside.

parts.label: Crankcase
parts.explanation: This hollow case supports the crankshaft and surrounds its moving parts.

parts.label: Rear bearing housing
parts.explanation: This sturdy seat holds the rear crankshaft bearing.

parts.label: Rear crankshaft bearing
parts.explanation: Balls between two rings let the shaft turn inside its support.

parts.label: Front bearing housing
parts.explanation: This support keeps the other end of the crankshaft aligned.

parts.label: Front crankshaft bearing
parts.explanation: This bearing supports the turning shaft next to the flywheel.

parts.label: Crank rotation frame
parts.explanation: The crankshaft and flywheel turn together.

angular_motion.label: Illustrative prescribed playback, 0.1 Hz; no additional slowdown

parts.label: Crankshaft
parts.explanation: Its off-centre pin connects to the rod, linking piston motion to rotation.

parts.label: Flywheel hub
parts.explanation: This bored centre joins the flywheel to the crankshaft.

parts.label: Flywheel
parts.explanation: This heavy wheel helps carry rotation between power strokes in a real engine.

parts.label: Piston
parts.explanation: Gas pressure pushes on its top. It slides inside the cylinder.

parts.label: Piston rings
parts.explanation: These rings help seal the gap between piston and cylinder.

parts.label: Piston pin
parts.explanation: This hollow pin lets the connecting rod swing inside the piston.

parts.label: Connecting rod
parts.explanation: This rigid link connects the piston pin to the crankshaft's off-centre pin.

parts.label: Rod bearing sleeves
parts.explanation: These hollow sleeves surround the two pins where the rod swings.

parts.label: Cylinder liner
parts.explanation: This smooth hollow sleeve guides the piston through its full stroke.

parts.label: Cylinder barrel
parts.explanation: The barrel supports the liner. Its outer ribs make the cylinder easy to recognize.

parts.label: Cylinder head
parts.explanation: The head closes the cylinder and holds the valves and spark plug.

parts.label: Intake valve
parts.explanation: This valve opens a route for fresh air and fuel into the cylinder.

parts.label: Exhaust valve
parts.explanation: This valve opens a route for burned gases to leave the cylinder.

parts.label: Valve seats and guides
parts.explanation: Seats seal against the valve heads. Hollow guides keep their stems aligned.

parts.label: Spark plug
parts.explanation: A spark starts burning near the end of compression, at the power-stroke boundary.

parts.label: Camshaft bearing supports
parts.explanation: Two supported bearings keep the camshaft aligned above the valves.

parts.label: Camshaft
parts.explanation: The camshaft turns once while the crankshaft turns twice. Its shaped lobes represent valve timing.

angular_motion.label: Illustrative prescribed playback, 0.05 Hz; no additional slowdown

parts.label: Timing connection
parts.explanation: This stationary diagram traces the connection that keeps cam and crank timing together.

parts.label: Cam cover
parts.explanation: This removable cover protects the valve-timing parts.

parts.label: Intake passage
parts.explanation: This hollow passage leads fresh mixture toward the intake valve.

parts.label: Exhaust passage
parts.explanation: This hollow passage carries burned gases away from the exhaust valve.

parts.label: Intake route cue
parts.explanation: A symbolic arrow shows inward flow when the intake valve is open, not a measured gas speed.

parts.label: Exhaust route cue
parts.explanation: A symbolic arrow shows outward flow when the exhaust valve is open, not a measured gas speed.

experiments.title: Link sliding to rotation
experiments.prompt: Start at 0 s. Predict how the piston and rod move as the crankshaft turns, then scrub to 2.5 s and compare piston position.
experiments.explanation: The cylinder guides the piston. The fixed-length rod connects its pin to the offset crankpin, linking sliding and rotation. Playback prescribes motion; it does not calculate forces. Inspection separation is not working motion.

experiments.title: Intake versus exhaust
experiments.prompt: Inspect intake at 2.5 s. Predict which valve and passage will be active at 17.5 s, then change the clock and compare.
experiments.explanation: During intake, the intake valve opens the inward mixture route. During exhaust, the exhaust valve opens the outward gas route. Shared phase flags coordinate valves and symbolic cues; gas flow is not calculated.

experiments.title: Compression versus power
experiments.prompt: Inspect compression at 7.5 s. Predict the valve states and piston travel during power, then scrub through 10 s to 12.5 s.
experiments.explanation: Both valves remain closed during compression and power. Ignition is marked at 10 s, cycle fraction 0.5, not throughout power. In a real engine, combustion raises pressure on the piston; the rod transmits force to the crankshaft. These forces are qualitative here.

experiments.title: One turn is not a complete cycle
experiments.prompt: Inspect 10 s after one crankshaft revolution. Predict how many more turns complete all four strokes, then scrub to 20 s and compare the cam angle.
experiments.explanation: Two crankshaft turns complete one four-stroke cycle while the camshaft turns once. The final endpoint retains the exhaust label. The flywheel helps carry real engines between power strokes, but this prescribed playback calculates neither stored energy nor self-sustaining operation.

controls.help: Scrub one four-stroke cycle to coordinate piston motion, valve states and cam rotation; playback is illustrative, not operating speed.

time_experiment.explanation: Starting at top dead centre, prescribed slider-crank kinematics drive two crank turns in 20 s and one cam turn. Ideal valve switching follows the same phase. Stop at cycle_duration. Preserve pause, reduced-motion, mobile, keyboard and inspection controls; never resume on idle.

coverage.explanation: Clock-driven slider-crank geometry links piston translation and rod swing to prescribed crankshaft and flywheel rotation within one cylinder.
The shared clock selects all four strokes across two crankshaft turns and one camshaft turn. Timing and playback rates are teaching assumptions.
Shared phase coordinates piston position, ideal valve states and symbolic flow routes. Ignition is annotated at fraction 0.5, not simulated as combustion or continuous sparking.

Inspect the pressure-to-piston-to-rod-to-crank force path and discuss flywheel inertia qualitatively. No quantitative torque, power, efficiency, pressure, emissions or thermal predictions are supported. Two-stroke exchange and detailed fuel delivery, lubrication and cooling remain excluded.

outcomes: Identify the cylinder, piston, connecting rod, crankshaft and flywheel; explain how piston motion and crankshaft rotation are connected.
Follow intake, compression, combustion/power and exhaust through a complete four-stroke cycle.
Connect piston position, valve states and ignition to air–fuel intake and exhaust flow.
Explain qualitatively how combustion pressure drives the piston and how rotational inertia helps carry the engine through non-power strokes.

generation_quality.scope: Recipe, label, connection and dependency checks only. Dependency paths do not prove numeric change. Overlap, recognizability, physical correctness and child usability require separate evaluation.

visual.scope: Eight fitted views; projected bounds, center-ray occlusion, conservative bounding-box overlaps and estimated two-line label capacity. These heuristics do not replace rendered-image or child usability review.

sampled_quality.scope: Defaults, five points per input plus presets, a midpoint context for apparently inactive controls, all-input endpoints, and lesson experiments. Finite geometry and observed changes only; no proof of scientific accuracy, recognizability or complete state-space coverage.
